category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a UK council booking service: public-sector form look with bold sans headings, one dark institutional green or blue, bordered red error summary titled 'There is a problem', summary card, single left-aligned column, no imagery. Predicted opposite: a friendly consumer booking look with rounded cards and illustration. The design matches the default element for element.

Overlap is near total; the only brief-driven choices are copy and the slot grid's Few left / Full states.

detector_comparison.notes: Zero hits is consistent with a clean, tell-free page; the absence of tells is not evidence of appeal. SLP-28 (emerald/teal sole accent) would not apply here in my reading: DESIGN.md says the green is the council's own hue. No post-unseal change to either verdict.

findings.title: Done page shows the reference but not the day, slot time or vehicle it was booked for
findings.description: The done page, which residents keep on their phone to show at the gate, carries only 'DR-204117', instructions and the 'At the centre' card. The booked day (Saturday 17 October), the 20-minute slot (09:20 to 09:40) and the vehicle (Car) shown on the confirm page are gone.
findings.impact: The page's single job is 'know the booking is made and what to show at the gate'; the gate checks the vehicle against the booking and the resident must arrive in the slot.

harm.statement: A resident opening the done page the next morning, or at the gate with poor signal, may not be able to see what time their slot is or which vehicle they booked, and may arrive at the wrong time or with the wrong vehicle and be turned away.

evidence.detail: Your reference card holds only the reference and two lines of text; no day/slot/vehicle anywhere on the page

findings.recommendation: Decide what the gate and the resident need together on this one screen (reference, day, slot time, vehicle, registration) and give it the hierarchy the gate reading requires.

findings.title: Cancelled booking is still headed 'Booked' and still promises a reminder
findings.description: In the cancelled state the h1 stays 'Booked', the reference is shown at full size, and the only signal is a small red bold line inside the card; the following lines still say 'Show this at the gate' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.'
findings.impact: The page's hierarchy says the opposite of its status.

harm.statement: A resident glancing at the page sees 'Booked' and a reference and may take the booking to be valid, then drive to the centre and be turned away because the booking is not on the gate's list.

evidence.detail: h1 'Booked'; red line 'Status: cancelled...' followed by 'Show this at the gate' and the reminder promise

findings.recommendation: Make the status the first thing the page says in the cancelled state and remove instructions that only apply to a live booking.

findings.title: Expired-slot state keeps 'Book this slot' as the primary and does not say what to do next
findings.description: The error summary says only 'This slot is no longer available.' The Slot row shows '–' beside a small 'Change slot' link, and the filled 'Book this slot' button remains the strongest element below a fully completed form.
findings.impact: The way forward (choose another slot) is the weakest element on the page; the primary points to an action that cannot succeed.

harm.statement: A resident whose held slot expired may press 'Book this slot' again or hunt for the small 'Change slot' link, slowing recovery when a scarce slot is at stake.

evidence.detail: error summary with no action; Slot '– · Change slot'; Book this slot unchanged at y≈1097

findings.recommendation: Decide what the one next step is when the hold has lapsed, make the message say it, and give that step the primary weight in this state.

findings.title: Few-left slots are pulled out of time order into an unlabelled band above 'Morning'
findings.description: On the when page the tiles with a 'Few left' chip (e.g. 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40 … 16:40 on Saturday) form their own band with no heading, above 'Morning' and 'Afternoon', which then list only the remaining times. A time such as 08:20 therefore does not appear under Morning.
findings.impact: Residents think in 'Saturday morning'; the grid's grouping no longer matches the time of day for a third of the slots.

harm.statement: A resident scanning 'Morning' for an early slot may not find 08:20 or 09:00 there and take them as unavailable, or not notice that the band above is also morning slots, and so pick a later slot than they could have had.

evidence.detail: unlabelled Few-left band; Morning row starts 08:00, 09:20, 10:00

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity or time of day organises the grid; if scarcity is shown, show it within the time order.

findings.title: Selected day and vehicle are marked only by a faint tint, weaker than unselected outlines
findings.description: The chosen day (Saturday 17) and the chosen vehicle (Van) get a very pale green fill and a slightly darker border, while every unselected option already has a bold green or dark outline. At 375 slot-chosen, 'Tomorrow' and 'Saturday 17' both appear tinted.
findings.impact: Day and vehicle are the two choices that decide whether the resident is let in.

harm.statement: A resident on a phone may not be sure which day or vehicle is chosen, and may book the wrong day or vehicle without noticing.

evidence.detail: Tomorrow and Saturday 17 both tinted; difference barely visible

findings.recommendation: Give the selected state of choice buttons a treatment that is stronger than the resting outline and unmistakable at phone size; check the Tomorrow tint is not a stray state.

findings.title: Permit field is shown before a vehicle is chosen, with no label saying who needs it
findings.description: On the vehicle page's default and errors states, with no vehicle chosen, 'Permit number' sits directly under the vehicle buttons with the hint 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.'; nothing in the label says it applies only to vans and cars with trailers. The rule appears only behind the bare circled-i button.
findings.impact: Most residents come by car and do not know about permits (context.md: 'Does not know: that vans and trailers need a permit').

harm.statement: A car owner may think they need a permit number they do not have and stop, while a van owner may not open the unlabelled info button that explains where the permit comes from.
harm.requirement: DESIGN.md Do's and Don'ts: 'Do state a rule where it applies.'

evidence.detail: Permit number field visible with no vehicle chosen; rule only in info panel (info-open state)

findings.recommendation: Decide when the permit field is relevant and state the van/trailer rule in the field's own label or hint.

findings.title: No identity or focal point of the recycling centre on any screen (sterile default)
findings.description: Every screen is a heading, a step line and bordered boxes on a pale ground; the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' and a 1.5px bin icon in the masthead. Nothing from the centre's world (Quarry Road, the gate, the waste streams residents sort into) is drawn on, and no element would be missed if moved to another council form.
findings.impact: Brand pair 'plain, not bare' drifts to bare; the identity floor that Operate surfaces still need is missing.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element taken from the centre's own mechanism (the gate check, the reference, the waste streams) that can recur quietly across the four steps without breaking Operate conventions.

findings.title: Wide widths leave the right half of the page empty while cards stretch with text in their left half
findings.description: At 1280 and 1440 the slot grid stops at about 820px and form columns at about 610px inside a 1184px container, while 'Opening days', 'Your booking' and 'Your reference' cards stretch full width with their text in the left half.
findings.impact: Desktop pages look unfinished and unbalanced; a design note, not a task harm.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width per step and make cards and controls share it.

findings.title: Narrow-width wraps split the registration example and strand words
findings.description: At 320 the confirm hint and error break 'AB12 / CDE' across lines, and 'it.' sits alone on the last line of the 'Nothing is paid' note; at 375 the footer phone number breaks '01632 / 960771'.
findings.impact: Small finish lapses on the phone widths most residents use; design note.
findings.recommendation: Keep registrations and phone numbers unbroken and balance short final lines.

strengths: Rules stated beside the controls they govern ('Rubble (up to four bags)', 'Mattresses (up to two)', permit format hint): keep.
Dark theme composed with its own greens and surfaces rather than inverted (1440-dark).
Copy voice of the gate attendant: brief, concrete, no exclamation marks; error messages say what to enter.
keep: Keep the one-filled-button-per-step structure and the rule-beside-control copy; any added identity must not dilute them.
notes: Independent subagent. Read only packet files, the role file, design-panel.md, brand-expression.md and (after unsealing) the SLP table of anti-slop.md. The first verdict write failed schema (strings instead of arrays) and was rewritten with identical verdicts after design.md had been read; values unchanged. Detector output had 0 hits. No baseline in packet, so pairwise not run (DES-05 not_applicable). Not assessable from stills: focus, hover, motion, toast, live slot updates.
